nodes.label: The hook — the lede, a consequence on their project

metadata.comment: The lifted .lesson-layout is a 2-column CSS grid (32px thread gutter + content); its ::before draws the thread. The runtime writes display:flex inline on a Group, so styleCss restates grid to win. Every child must be a DIRECT child of this box — the Sprint-8 fragment contract — which is why the section rows come from a For Each placed here rather than inside a wrapper.

A wrapped row of content-sized chips (the layout-wrap-a-row-of-content-width-items recipe): each chip keeps its own width and flows to the next line, which is what a stepper wants at 390px. The validator's Columns suggestion is for grids of equal cells, which this is not.

nodes.label: The active step's sections, as knots

metadata.comment: Empty means the first step. Set by a chip or by the step close; nothing else writes it.
The repeater surfaces the chip's `select` as itemOutputSignal-select and the row's id as itemActionItemId; the id IS the step id.

nodes.label: Changing step starts at the top

metadata.comment: The one thing a node cannot do. Runs only on the signal.

One instance per page. Its `copy` output is the whole bundle; Logic/Sections for step puts it on every row, and the For Each maps it onto Section row's Copy input by name. Delete this node and the lesson still renders — in the English the kit ships (TASK-L160). A lesson is the learner's surface. When a coach can read one, this is the line that changes — one word, in the instance, rather than a flag threaded through the kit (TASK-L163 §3).
Was the literal "Concept · woven onto your project" on ls_eyebrow.text. It lives in Data/Strings now (TASK-L161).
Why a JavaScript node and not a wire to Page.title: the port is build-time. See the script.

nodes.label: language — from the one owner in App

metadata.comment: A TRANSPORT, NEVER A SECOND DECISION. `Data/Strings` is instantiated once per surface that needs the kit's copy object, and a component cannot wire across to another, so the resolved language is broadcast through this named Variable. The one OWNER is still the `i18next` node in App: this node only carries its answer. Every `/Data/Strings` instance in the project learns the language exactly this way — TASK-L162 §2.

The fixture was one lesson and the page never had to say which. The backend holds one per concept, so every link to this page passes the concept it names: the up-next card and the dossier's lesson link on /course (TASK-L171 §0b). A query parameter rather than a path one so /lesson with no concept is still a page, not a 404.

Sprint 49 decision 7 promised this: Sam's next step has no lesson written for it until the engine sprint, and the up-next card opens it. MOUNTED, never visible (L157): visibility keeps the space. No colour of its own and no warning tone — a lesson not written yet is not something the learner did wrong.

nodes.label: Their own programme — for the work they sent in

metadata.comment: reader: learner, exactly as /course places it (TASK-L182). The product's lesson page reads /api/course too (L59, L118); here it is for one thing — what the learner sent in against this lesson's challenge, and what came back.

parameters.functionScript:
/*
 * A LESSON OPENS WITH NOTHING SAVED SINCE IT OPENED (TASK-L177).
 * `dbtCapturedFacts` is what the learner saved on THIS page since it opened, laid
 * over the facts the page loaded. A Variable outlives its page, so it is emptied
 * whenever the page is told which lesson it is — the facts the page loads are
 * the backend's, and they already hold everything saved before.
 */
Noodl.Variables.dbtCapturedFacts = {};
